question.problem:
Write the following series in sigma notation in terms of index $n.$

$5-\frac{5}{3}+\frac{5}{9}+…={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }${{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The first term is ${a}_{1}=5$ and the second term is ${a}_{2}=-\frac{5}{3}.$ Using these two terms, we compute the common ratio:

$$
r=\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}}=\frac{(-\frac{5}{3})}{5}=-\frac{1}{3}
$$

Therefore, the general term can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}{(r)}^{n-1} \\  & =5{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{n-1} \\  & =5{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{-1}{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{n} \\  & =5(-3){(-\frac{1}{3})}^{n} \\  & =(-15){(-\frac{1}{3})}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the infinite geometric series can be written in sigma notation as

$$
\begin{aligned}5-\frac{5}{3}+\frac{5}{9}+⋯ & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,(-15){(-\frac{1}{3})}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$
